topic.examWeightHint: This is the question that opens the paper. On Summer 2024 it was Q1 at Higher and Q6 at Foundation, worth 5 marks: two structures to name from a diagram [2], two functions [2] and the job of the flagellum [1]. sheet.howExamined: B2, 1 hour 15 minutes: 70 marks at Foundation, 80 at Higher, calculator allowed. This is usually the settling-in question at the very start of the paper, worth about 5 marks: a diagram with two or three parts to name for [1] each, then two functions for [1] each. The same question runs on both tiers. Marks are single [1] lines with tight accept lists, and a name written beside a function is marked as well, so a wrong name can cancel a right function.
traps: Giving the prostate gland's function less thought than the testis's: the prostate was the weaker of the two on both tiers, and any answer for either that drifted into urine earned nothing (Summer 2024 B2 Higher Q1 and B2 Foundation Q6)

Reading a letter off a female-system diagram and giving its neighbour: on Summer 2023 B2 Higher Q1 most candidates found the part where ovulation happens, and fewer found the part that is lost when fertilisation does not occur
Spending too long on the names: on Summer 2025 B2 Higher Q6 most candidates named the organs correctly and the marks went elsewhere in the same question, so bank these and move on
Writing ureter where urethra was meant (Summer 2024 B2, both tiers)
Naming a structure that was not asked for, and naming it loosely (Summer 2024 B2, both tiers)
Swapping the ovary and the oviduct
Calling the vagina the cervix, or the cervix the vagina

items.stem: Before we start, three things you have already met in B1. Which level of organisation is a group of organs working together?

options.feedback: An organ system. The male and female reproductive systems are exactly that.
A tissue is a group of similar cells. Organs are built from tissues.
An organ is one structure made of several tissues. A group of organs working together is the next level up.
An organism is the whole living thing, made of several organ systems.

items.stem: Which part of a cell holds the chromosomes?

options.feedback: The nucleus. Later in this unit you will meet a cell whose nucleus carries only half a set.
The cytoplasm is where most reactions happen, but the chromosomes are kept in the nucleus.
The membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
Mitochondria release energy by respiration. You will meet them again in the sperm cell.
The kidney. Keep that in mind: nothing in the reproductive system makes urine.
The bladder stores urine; it does not make it.
The liver makes urea, which the kidney then puts into urine, but the urine itself is made in the kidney.
The ureter is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.

items.skill: Name the site of sperm production

options.feedback: The testes. They also make testosterone.
The prostate gland adds fluid to sperm that have already been made.
The sperm tube carries sperm; it does not make them.
The scrotum is the sac. What it holds is the testes, and those are where the sperm are made.

items.stem: Which tube carries both semen and, at other times, urine?
items.skill: Tell the urethra from the ureter

options.feedback: The urethra. It is the only tube in the body that does both jobs.
The ureter runs from the kidney to the bladder and carries urine only. The two words are nearly the same, so the examiner reads the spelling closely.
The sperm tube carries sperm only, and only as far as the prostate gland.
The oviduct is part of the female system.

items.stem: In which part of the female reproductive system does fertilisation take place?

options.feedback: The oviduct. The ovum is fertilised on its way from the ovary to the uterus.
The uterus is where the ball of cells implants afterwards, not where the nuclei fuse.
The ovary releases the ovum. Fertilisation happens after the ovum has left it.
The cervix is the ring of muscle at the base of the uterus.

items.stem: What does the prostate gland do?
items.skill: Give the function of the prostate gland

options.text: it adds fluid to the sperm
options.feedback: It adds fluid to the sperm. Sperm and that fluid together are semen.
Urine is made in the kidney. The reports say answers here drift towards urine more than anything else.
Sperm are made in the testes. By the time the sperm reach the prostate gland they are complete.

options.text: it stores sperm until they are needed
options.feedback: Storage is not the job the specification gives it. It adds fluid.

items.stem: Why are the testes held in the scrotum, outside the body?
items.skill: Explain the position of the testes

options.text: because it is cooler there than inside the body
options.feedback: Cooler. Sperm are made best a little below body temperature.

options.text: because there is more room outside the body
options.feedback: Room is not the reason. Temperature is.

options.text: because sperm could not leave the body otherwise
options.feedback: Sperm leave along the sperm tube and the urethra, whatever the position of the testes.

options.text: because the scrotum makes the sperm
options.feedback: The scrotum is a sac of skin; it makes nothing. The testes inside it make the sperm.

items.stem: Which structure is the ring of muscle between the uterus and the vagina?

options.feedback: The cervix, the neck of the uterus.
The vagina is the passage below the cervix, not the ring of muscle itself.
The oviducts join the uterus at the top, not the bottom.
The urethra carries urine out of the body and is not part of the female reproductive system.

items.stem: A diagram is printed at half life size. A structure measures 30 mm on the diagram. How long is it really?
items.skill: Use a scale to find a real length

options.feedback: 60 mm. At half life size the drawing is half the real length, so the real length is twice the drawing.
That is the drawn length multiplied by the magnification. Half life size means the real thing is the bigger one, so divide.
That is the length on the paper. The scale has not been used at all.
That is the drawn length multiplied by ten, which is a unit change rather than the scale.

parts.stem:
A textbook prints a diagram of the female reproductive system at half life size.

parts.workedSolution: Sperm are made in the testis. The testes hang in the scrotum, a sac outside the body, because sperm are made best at a temperature a little below body temperature. prompts.answer: Testis, scrotum, sperm tube, prostate gland, urethra and penis.

prompts.prompt: What does the prostate gland do?

prompts.prompt: The urethra and the ureter are two different tubes. What does each one carry, and where does it run?
prompts.answer: The urethra carries semen and, at other times, urine, and runs from the bladder out through the penis. The ureter carries urine only, from the kidney down to the bladder.

prompts.prompt: Name the five parts of the female reproductive system the specification lists.
prompts.answer: Ovary, oviduct, uterus, cervix and vagina.

prompts.prompt: Where does fertilisation happen, and where does the ball of cells settle afterwards?
prompts.answer: Fertilisation happens in the oviduct. The ball of cells settles into the lining of the uterus.

prompts.prompt: Why are the testes held in the scrotum, outside the body?
prompts.answer: Because it is cooler outside the body, and sperm are made best at a temperature a little below body temperature.
